articles.title: T. Rowe Price CEO Sharps on Private Assets and AI Adoption
articles.summary: T. Rowe Price CEO Rob Sharps discusses how the company is adapting to the rise of passive investing. articles.summary: The OpenClaw Foundation has released version 2.0 of its open-source AI platform, its largest release to date with over 16,000 pull requests. New features include cloud sessions on rented machines, real-time collaboration, and a browser app rebuilt from scratch. The software now automatically detects existing resources like API keys and AI subscriptions during setup. articles.title: AI Adoption Is Finally Showing Up in Fundamentals
articles.summary: Michelle Weaver, head of US thematic research at Morgan Stanley, says companies are beginning to see measurable benefits from AI as adoption moves from experimentation into production. About 25% of S&P 500 companies are now quantifying benefits from AI, up from 14% a year ago, with AI adopters also seeing relative forward margin expansion. “You’re starting to see this come into the fundamentals.” This interview aired Aug. 27, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Stop Building Chatbots: Why Enterprise Engineering is Shifting to Agentic Workflows
articles.summary: Most enterprise AI initiatives fail. Companies spend hundreds of thousands of USD bolting a chat interface onto a proprietary database and call it innovation. But here is the hard truth: business users do not want to chat with their data. They want the data to execute the work. We have reached the peak of the "ChatGPT wrapper" era. The next evolution of enterprise software is not generative. It is agentic. The Chatbot Illusion If you look at the internal AI tools built by mid-market and enterprise companies over the last two years, they almost all look the same. They are passive conversational agents. A user asks a question, the system retrieves a document using RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), and the AI summarizes it. This is helpful for research, but it creates zero operational leverage. articles.title: Giving AI Agents a Deterministic Clock (Zero LLM in the Loop)
articles.summary: When building autonomous AI systems, developers eventually hit a fundamental architectural wall. Your coding agent asks you a question, and you step away from the keyboard. Today, nothing happens. The session hangs, the question rots, and the work stalls. At J. Servo LLC, we architect enterprise AI systems to operate predictably. We built Sundial to act as the missing half of the human-in-the-loop framework[cite: 1]. It operates on a single defining principle: Sundial measures absence, not time[cite: 1]. When the human becomes the blocker, the agent's clock keeps running[cite: 1]. It nudges you on your desktop, escalates politely through your absence, and greets you with continuity upon your return[cite: 1]. If you never answer, the agent proceeds on its stated judgment or stands down[cite: 1]. It does this deterministically, with zero model calls, and runs 100% locally[cite: 1]. articles.title: Google Says Gemini App Has Surpassed 1 Billion Monthly Active Users, Its Fastest-Growing Product
articles.summary: Google says the Gemini app has surpassed 1 billion monthly active users, making it the fastest-growing product in the company's history. The milestone is more than a large user count. It shows how Google's strategy of placing Gemini across familiar products and devices is turning an AI assistant into a widely used consumer interface for voice, visual and multimodal tasks. In its official Gemini app milestone announcement, Google points to several indicators of how that adoption is taking shape: voice is used by roughly 63% of Gemini app users, more than 150 million images are generated daily, and the app has more than 100 million active iOS users. Google also says Gemini has more than 40 integrations across Android, the web and other surfaces. For businesses, the immediate lesson is not that every Gemini interaction is a workflow automation.
